findings.description: Orders, balances, positions, and transactions have no owner/account binding. A differently identified principal with a tool-level capability can read shared portfolio state, cancel another principal's order, or transfer shared funds.
findings.preconditions: Multiple principals share an ExecutionGateway or its backing resource state; the attacker has the relevant coarse capability.
findings.violated_invariant: Capabilities must authorize a principal over a specific resource domain, not only a tool name.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant disclosure and mutation of financial state.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: None; the original dataset uses one fixed identity and one isolated sandbox per scenario.
findings.remediation_direction: Model account/resource ownership explicitly and enforce subject-resource-action checks at both lookup and mutation boundaries.

findings.description: Two ApprovalManager instances loaded from the same approved ledger can each consume and execute the same approval. Per-instance locking does not provide globally single-use consumption.
findings.preconditions: Two workers or manager instances load the same ledger before either observes the other's update.
findings.violated_invariant: One approval must authorize at most one execution globally.
findings.impact: A high-risk approved withdrawal/action can execute more than once.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: The benchmark uses a simulated verifier; existing concurrency tests share one manager instance.
findings.remediation_direction: Use an atomic compare-and-consume operation in one durable coordination store with a uniqueness/transaction guarantee.

findings.description: Audit confidentiality, integrity, and terminal completeness can all fail: access_key and secrets nested through tuples remain visible; in-memory event payloads share mutable nested state; and a post-execution recorder failure leaves the side effect committed with no EXECUTED event.
findings.preconditions: A secret reaches raw request arguments, a caller retains a mutable returned decision object, or the recorder fails after execution.
findings.violated_invariant: Audit evidence must be confidential, immutable, and complete for protected execution.
findings.impact: Credential disclosure and unreliable forensic/accounting evidence.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: Post-execution atomicity is documented, but these concrete confidentiality and mutation paths are not benchmarked.
findings.remediation_direction: Adopt schema-based recursive secret handling, deep-copy/freeze recorded events, and use a transactional outbox or explicit reconciliation state for terminal audit.

findings.description: orders.cancel accepts only order_id and its tool definition has no symbol field, so an allowed_symbols constraint is not enforced when cancelling an order outside the grant's symbol scope.
findings.preconditions: The caller knows an open order ID and holds orders.cancel constrained to another symbol.
findings.violated_invariant: Symbol constraints must apply to every scoped resource action.
findings.impact: Unauthorized cancellation outside the granted market scope.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: None; cancellation is tested only as a benign unscoped workflow.
findings.remediation_direction: Resolve the target resource before authorization and enforce its symbol/owner attributes against capability scope.

findings.description: Repeated trace/request identifiers and provider call IDs are not idempotency keys. Identical transfers execute twice, and a call_id reused on a later model turn also executes twice.
findings.preconditions: Retry, replay, duplicated delivery, or a provider emitting the same call identifier across turns.
findings.violated_invariant: A duplicated financial command identifier should not create a second side effect.
findings.impact: Duplicate financial operations during retries or replay.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: Approval replay is tested; ordinary request/call replay is not.
findings.remediation_direction: Define durable idempotency semantics and reject or return the prior result for duplicate subject/action keys.

findings.description: The approval digest binds agent_id, tool, and normalized arguments but not principal or environment. Keeping agent_id constant permits a sandbox approval to execute under another principal or production-labelled context.
findings.preconditions: The integration permits principal/environment changes while retaining the same agent_id and an unconstrained capability.
findings.violated_invariant: Approval must bind all security-relevant execution identity and context.
findings.impact: Approved authority can cross principal or environment boundaries.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: The original identity test changes agent_id only.
findings.remediation_direction: Include canonical principal, environment, resource/account, policy version, and relevant state in the approval subject/digest.

findings.description: Per-call capabilities permit unsafe compositions and capability-valid maliciously induced actions: repeated boundary orders, cross-tool aggregate spend, unrestricted destinations, and injected in-scope cancellation all execute.
findings.preconditions: The attacker can influence an agent that already possesses individually sufficient capabilities.
findings.violated_invariant: Operational mandates may require aggregate, destination, resource, or trusted-intent constraints beyond per-call authorization.
findings.impact: Policy-compliant calls can combine into financially harmful outcomes.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: A07/A09 disclose the basic limitation, but the independent cases show broader cross-tool, destination, and cancellation consequences.
findings.remediation_direction: Add trusted mandates, destination allowlists, resource scope, rolling budgets, and approval escalation where product requirements demand intent safety.

findings.description: The fixed benchmark metrics are internally correct, but many named prompt-injection/privilege categories collapse to identical scripted missing-capability checks. The approval oracle reads scenario metadata directly, the seed does not control any stochastic operation, and end-to-end paths are not like-for-like across configurations.
findings.preconditions: Generalizing fixed-dataset scores to broad attack-class resistance or comparative runtime performance.
findings.violated_invariant: Security evaluation should separate nominal labels from materially distinct enforcement paths and comparable workloads.
findings.impact: The 12.5% original ASR is reliable for the fixed scenarios but weak evidence for unseen attack classes.
findings.original_benchmark_coverage: Intrinsic to the original method and partly disclosed in failure-analysis.md.
findings.remediation_direction: Use externally authored scenarios, real approval-state paths, materially distinct attacks, repeated trials, and comparable timing boundaries.

findings.description: The repository has an unborn main branch and no Git commits, so claims that the final artifact is committed and that no post-freeze tuning occurred cannot be independently established from version history.
findings.preconditions: Reliance on repository history for freeze or artifact provenance.
findings.violated_invariant: A frozen benchmark release needs immutable, attributable provenance.
findings.impact: The artifact contents can be verified, but the historical freeze claim cannot.
findings.remediation_direction: Create a signed/tagged commit containing code, dataset fingerprint, artifact, and validation report.
